name: NT-PRO BNP
description: NT-proBNP measures N-terminal pro-brain natriuretic peptide and evaluates heart failure severity, prognosis, and response to therapy. This cardiac biomarker helps diagnose and monitor congestive heart failure.

testdetails.instrumentation: Abbott Architect, Roche Elecsys, Beckman Coulter

literatureReview: NT-proBNP is released from cardiac ventricles in response to myocardial stretch and stress. Normal <125 pg/mL (age-dependent). Elevated levels indicate heart failure, left ventricular dysfunction, and cardiac strain. Higher levels correlate with worse prognosis and disease severity. Chemiluminescent immunoassay provides excellent precision. Used in heart failure diagnosis, risk stratification, and monitoring treatment response. More stable than BNP with longer half-life. Age-specific cutoffs: <75 years <125 pg/mL, 75-80 years <200 pg/mL, >80 years <300 pg/mL. Also elevated in renal failure, pulmonary hypertension, and acute coronary syndromes. Critical biomarker for heart failure management and prognosis assessment.
